assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean, general statistical-physics idea: collective motion of self-propelled agents is an ordered non-equilibrium phase, with a flocking transition (Vicsek model), hydrodynamic theory showing long-range order even in two dimensions (Toner-Tu), and the hydrodynamics of active fluids and giant number fluctuations (Ramaswamy and coworkers). It shows how a simple mechanism produces universal behaviour across birds, bacteria and colloids, and it connects theory to experiment in a way I value.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek introduced the minimal model, Toner and Tu supplied the continuum theory and the symmetry-breaking argument that overturns the Mermin-Wagner expectation, and Ramaswamy developed the hydrodynamics of active matter. The three supplied names map onto three distinct decisive contributions. Other contributors (e.g. Tu, Marchetti, Cates) are not in the credited set and I cannot add them.
assessment.maturity: Roughly three decades of development, with quantitative experiments (vibrated granular layers, colloidal rollers, bacterial suspensions) that confirm several predictions, though not all. The field is mature enough for recognition and still vigorous.
uncertainties: Experimental confirmation of the exact Toner-Tu exponents is partial and debated.
Whether the prize would be seen as physics of the living or of the non-equilibrium state is a framing question.
Credit for Yu-Tu-Toner theory (Tu is not on the list) leaves a gap I cannot resolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a paradigmatic non-equilibrium universality class, with exact solutions connecting to random-matrix (Tracy-Widom) statistics, which I find especially attractive. It has been confirmed in turbulent liquid-crystal experiments and other systems. Its reach into mathematics, interface growth, and random matrices makes it a lasting contribution.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the equation; Parisi is not in the supplied credited names and, as a laureate already, does not matter here. Kardar and Zhang are the natural pair. Spohn is a mathematical physicist who made the exact-solution and universality results rigorous, which is a different kind of contribution, so I would include him only as a third name; a two-person configuration is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Exact solutions and several experiments (Takeuchi-Sano) are strong and independent, but the connection to experiments in generic growth settings is more mixed.
uncertainties: Whether the exact-solution contributions (Spohn, Corwin, Sasamoto, Amir, Quastel, Balazs) are a part of the same prize is open.
Broad experimental universality is less clean than the theory suggests.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices became a controllable quantum simulator of Hubbard physics: the superfluid-Mott transition, single-site-resolved microscopy and programmable many-body Hamiltonians. The science is both original and widely used to test models of strongly correlated matter, and in effect it is statistical mechanics made experimental.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, Greiner (with Bloch and Hänsch) observed the Mott transition, and Bloch and Greiner developed quantum gas microscopy. Esslinger's Fermi-Hubbard work is also decisive and the cap of three forces an uncomfortable exclusion. Jaksch and Hänsch are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and well replicated across many groups. Recognition is timely but overlaps conceptually with prior cold-atom prizes (1997, 2001), which committee members would weigh.
uncertainties: Who among Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger should be excluded is unresolved.
Overlap with the earlier BEC prize and with the credit for Zoller in other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure theory with molecular dynamics and made ab initio simulation of liquids, solids and chemical reactions routine. It is a methodological invention with enormous lasting impact, in a field the Prize recognised in 1998 and 2013 for related computational chemistry. Computational method prizes are rarer in physics, but the 2024 and 2021 prizes show openness to methods that change how physics is done.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper has exactly two authors and credit is unambiguous. A two-person prize is simple and fair.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use and thousands of derivative applications. The method is extremely mature; the concern is timeliness against whether the committee regards it as physics or chemistry.
uncertainties: Whether it falls in physics or chemistry as a prize category.
Whether the 1998 Kohn prize partially covered this field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter. This is a rare case in which a clear theory preceded and guided a dramatic experiment, and it started a large, productive field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 discovery with Cao and Fatemi. Pablo's graduate student Yuan Cao is not credited. The three names fit a theory-plus-experiment prize, but several other contributors (e.g. Dean, Kim, Yazdani, Young, Efetov) are important.
assessment.maturity: Only about eight years old. The experiments have been replicated, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and the correlated states is still unsettled, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The microscopic origin of superconductivity is still debated.
Credit extends beyond three people, including the doctoral student who led the experiment.
Likely premature relative to other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, delivers fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 and makes tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second feasible. The idea is simple and the physics is understood, and the instrument is a long-lasting reference tool.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance to the best levels with strontium and the many-body spin-exchange understanding. A two-person prize is natural. Hall and Hänsch (2005, combs) and Wineland (2012, ion clocks) overlap the field already.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well confirmed by many laboratories, and timely in view of the pending redefinition of the second.
uncertainties: Whether Hall and Hänsch's prior prize partly covers the enabling frequency comb.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming transition places glasses, foams, grains and emulsions into one critical framework with isostaticity and marginal stability, giving universal exponents and a good example of a simple mechanism behind messy disordered matter. This is close to my own intellectual taste, though the experimental case is less decisive.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram and Wyart contributed isostaticity and the marginal-stability picture. O'Hern, Silbert and Witten are not credited, and their numerical work was decisive; the three names are reasonable but leave out some important contributors.
assessment.maturity: About twenty years old and widely used, but experimental verification of the critical exponents in real systems is limited, and the link to the glass transition remains disputed.
uncertainties: Relevance of the zero-temperature critical point to real thermal glasses is debated.
Credit for the original simulations is split among people not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and the experimental detection in HgTe quantum wells launched topological matter as a central theme of modern condensed-matter physics, with a clear conceptual picture based on Z2 invariants. It is highly original and has had lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original proposal and Z2 classification, and Molenkamp's group made the experimental observation, building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not credited here). The configuration is plausible but contentious. The 2016 prize already honoured topological phases (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz), which complicates the argument for novelty.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed and mature, but the 2016 prize and the BHZ credit give a degree of overlap and an unresolved allocation.
uncertainties: The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is missing from the credit.
